title: Frontends must design their own limited-filtering strategy, trading resilience against accessibility
content:
A.5.4.1.3.2 requires frontends to "develop internal processes to determine their strategy for limited filtering, to ensure optimal balance of resilience and accessibility," while A.5.4.1.1 obliges actors to "actively explore and implement reasonably available options" to reduce exposure.

The Atlas prescribes the *outcome* and leaves the *mechanism* to operators. This is deliberate for a decentralized frontend set: a single mandated filtering method would become a single point of failure and a uniform target, and would age badly as IP-geolocation techniques change.

The cost is uneven enforcement — 'reasonably available' and 'optimal balance' are judgment standards, so two compliant frontends may filter very differently. A.5.4.1.2's penalty clause therefore has to be applied against an unspecified baseline.
description: A.5.4.1.3.2 delegates the how of IP filtering to each frontend operator, requiring internal processes rather than prescribing a shared list or method.
